title: Faith: what it is and how it grows
share: What is faith, and how does it grow? Ten steps from Hebrews 11 and Abraham to the mustard seed, and faith and works side by side.
opening_question: What is faith, and how does it grow? Read what Hebrews says faith is, how Abraham believed, how faith comes, what Yeshua said to the father who cried "help thou mine unbelief", and what Paul and James say about faith and works, side by side. Each step asks what the text says and what it means for me.

steps.question: How does Hebrews describe faith? What does it call "the substance of things hoped for", and what does faith let us understand about how the worlds were made?
steps.apply: What am I hoping for that I cannot see yet?

facts.text: "faith" is pistis: "persuasion", "moral conviction", and also "constancy". The King James also translates it "assurance" and "fidelity".
"substance" is hypostasis: "a setting under (support)", "assurance". Faith is what stands under the hope.
"evidence" is elenchos: "proof, conviction". The BSB reads "certainty".
Faith reaches back to creation too: "Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God".

steps.question: What did Abel and Enoch do "by faith", and what two things must the one who comes to God believe?
steps.apply: Do I seek God diligently, or only when I need something?

facts.text: Abel "offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain", and "by it he being dead yet speaketh".
Enoch "had this testimony, that he pleased God".
"without faith it is impossible to please him". The one who comes "must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him."

steps.question: What did the LORD tell Abram to look at, and what was "counted" to him? How does Paul describe Abraham's faith when he was "about an hundred years old"?
steps.apply: Which promise of God am I tempted to stagger at because it looks impossible?

facts.text: "believed" in Genesis 15:6 is aman: "to build up or support", to "render (or be) firm or faithful", to "trust or believe". The same root gives the word Amen.
Abram was told: "Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars". Then: "he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness."
Paul: "against hope believed in hope". "He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God".

steps.question: When the LORD answered Habakkuk, what did He say about the vision that tarries, and how shall the just live?
steps.apply: What am I waiting for, and can I keep living by faith while it tarries?

facts.text: "though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come".
"faith" in Habakkuk 2:4 is emunah: "literally firmness", "security", "moral fidelity". It is steadiness, holding on.
Paul quotes Habakkuk: "as it is written, The just shall live by faith." Hebrews 10:38 and Galatians 3:11 quote it too.

steps.question: According to Paul, how does faith come? What does it come by, and what does the hearing come by?
steps.apply: How much of God's word do I actually hear in a week?

facts.text: "hearing" is akoe: "hearing (the act, the sense or the thing heard)". Faith comes from what is heard.
The KJV and the Ethiopian Canon read "the word of God"; the BSB reads "the word of Christ". Greek manuscripts differ here.

steps.question: What did the father of the boy say to Yeshua, what did Yeshua answer, and what did the father cry "with tears"?
steps.apply: Can I bring my unbelief to Him honestly, as this father did?

facts.text: The father said "if thou canst do any thing". Yeshua turned the "if" around: "If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth."
"Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief." "unbelief" is apistia: "faithlessness", "disbelief". The father had both at once, and Yeshua still healed his son.
To the disciples: "This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting." The BSB reads only "by prayer"; the KJV and the Ethiopian Canon add "fasting".

steps.question: Why could the disciples not cast the spirit out? What did Yeshua say a little faith, "as a grain of mustard seed", can do? What did the apostles ask Him?
steps.apply: Is my faith too small, or is it resting on something too small?

facts.text: "Because of your unbelief". Then: "If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence".
The apostles asked: "Increase our faith." The answer was about the mustard seed and "this sycamine tree".
The power is not in the size of the faith: "nothing shall be impossible unto you" is said of faith as small as a seed.

steps.question: Why did Yeshua marvel at the centurion? And when Peter walked on the water, what made him begin to sink?
steps.apply: When I see the wind, where do my eyes go?

facts.text: The centurion: "speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed." Yeshua: "I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel."
"as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee."
Peter "walked on the water". "But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid". Yeshua "caught him" and said "O thou of little faith": oligopistos, "lacking confidence".

steps.question: Read Paul and James side by side. What does Paul say we are saved by, and what are we created for? What does James say about "faith without works"?
steps.apply: Where can someone see my faith this week?

facts.text: Paul: "by grace are ye saved through faith", "Not of works, lest any man should boast". And in the next verse: "created in Christ Jesus unto good works".
James: "faith without works is dead", and "by works a man is justified, and not by faith only." Both Paul and James quote the same verse about Abraham.
"justified" is dikaioo: "to render (i.e. show or regard as) just or innocent".

Christians read these two passages in different ways. Some say Paul speaks of how a person is made right with God and James of how faith shows itself. Others say faith and works together justify. Some say both. Each reading points to these same verses; BibleChat gives no verdict.

steps.question: How does Paul describe the life he now lives, and how do believers walk? Who does Hebrews say to look to in the race?
steps.apply: What weight do I need to lay aside, and where are my eyes fixed?

facts.text: Paul: "the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me."
"we walk by faith, not by sight".
After the list of Hebrews 11 comes "so great a cloud of witnesses". The race is run "Looking unto" the "author and finisher of our faith".

remember.text: "faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen."
"without faith it is impossible to please him"
Abraham "believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness."
"the just shall live by his faith."
"faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God."
"Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief."
"by grace are ye saved through faith", and "faith without works is dead".
"we walk by faith, not by sight"
